line: You could throw out every expensive foundation on your shelf right now, and you would not lose a thing. Because not one of them was ever going to work on your skin. And I can show you exactly why in about thirty seconds.

concepts.frame1: she stands square to the lens holding a plain beige foundation bottle in one hand and the closed violet FACELOVE stick in the other, two shelves of forty unlabelled bottles behind her
concepts.stakes: every bottle behind her was a waste
concepts.where: her dressing room, at the shelves
concepts.turn: '…not one of them was ever going to work' — her eyes flick to the shelf

concepts.frame1: she pulls one bottle off the crowded shelf and drops it into a wastebasket at her feet without looking
concepts.where: her dressing room, at the shelves
concepts.turn: she turns to the lens: 'You could throw out every…'

concepts.frame1: a slow slide along the row of forty bottles, each a slightly different wrong beige
close on her bare tired face, then she lifts the stick into frame
concepts.turn: the stick in frame on 'thirty seconds'

concepts.frame1: a department-store beauty counter, her bag full of bottles
concepts.turn: cut to the shelf at home

line: I spent years blaming my skin for every foundation on this shelf. It turns out it was never my skin at all.

concepts.frame1: close on her fingertip running along the crowded shelf, tapping bottle after bottle, every one a slightly different wrong beige, until it stops on the last and she looks up at the lens
concepts.stakes: years and money on the wrong shades
concepts.turn: '…never my skin at all' — straight into 'I am fifty seven'

concepts.frame1: her bare tired face in the hand mirror, the shelf behind her reflected
concepts.turn: she lowers the mirror to the lens

concepts.frame1: an armful of bottles tipped onto the white dresser
concepts.turn: she picks the stick out of the pile

concepts.frame1: she shakes her head at the shelf, arms folded
a receipt pinned to the shelf edge

line: Watch what happens when I paint this wall with one factory color. Because this is exactly what your foundation is doing to your face.

concepts.frame1: low and wide: the roller drags one long stripe of flat pinkish beige up the bare warm plaster wall, plainly the wrong colour, and she turns to the lens with the roller in hand
concepts.stakes: the wrong colour, plain as day
concepts.turn: '…what your foundation is doing to your face' — cut to the caked macro

concepts.frame1: macro: beige paint sinking into the wall's hairline cracks
concepts.turn: the same pattern on her cheek

concepts.frame1: she pops the lid off the plain paint can and holds it up beside her face
concepts.stakes: the colour is wrong for her

concepts.frame1: the paint can and the foundation bottle side by side on the drop cloth
she stands beside the wall, arms folded, unimpressed
